notes: No breadboard is used; the manual solders wires directly to the Nano Every pads and module pins, so jumper-wire nodes are used with solder joints.
The catalogue types led-strip, ds3231-rtc/ds1307-rtc and bme280 have no usable ports, so new types (ws2812b-strip-8, ds3231-module, bme280-breakout) were defined with named ports.
The DS3231 module pass-through is modelled as two port sets (.1 = side wired to the Nano, .2 = side wired to the BME280) joined internally per signal.
The manual does not say which Nano GND pad is used. GND.1 goes to the RTC and GND.2 to the LED strip; this is an assumption.
The manual says the LED strip GND is wired but does not name the pad. It is assumed to go to a Nano GND pin.
Power comes from USB. The Nano Every catalogue entry has no USB port, so the USB cable is not modelled.
The 3D-printed gnome enclosure and the strip's DOUT end are not modelled. DOUT is left unconnected.
The RTC and BME280 are wired in parallel on the same I2C bus (3V3, GND, A4/SDA, A5/SCL) through the RTC pass-through pins.
